subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session systemEvent cron jobs support a first-class model/provider override, and what single public API shape should own it?
rationale: The request changes public cron protocol and main-session provider/session routing semantics, so automation should not choose between `payload.model`, top-level job fields, or a `sessionOverride` contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add one canonical cron run override
options.body: Define a single job-level override contract, route it through allowlist/fallback validation, and pass it to heartbeat/session execution without contextKey encoding.

options.title: Reuse payload.model on systemEvent
options.body: Extend `systemEvent` payloads with `model` as the smallest schema change, accepting that event text payloads now carry run-routing metadata.

options.title: Keep main systemEvent default-only
options.body: Document that cheaper per-cron models require isolated `agentTurn` jobs and leave main-session systemEvent jobs on the session/default model.

recommendation.title: Add one canonical cron run override
recommendation.body: Define a single job-level override contract, route it through allowlist/fallback validation, and pass it to heartbeat/session execution without contextKey encoding.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron protocol, types, and main execution path blame to Vincent Koc's recent maintenance refactor, making him the best code-path owner for the API decision packet.
